description: Scale computer-use 2.0 with open-source drivers, cross-OS sandboxes, and benchmarks for training, evaluation, and data generation.

summary.one_liner: Cua is a computer-use agent platform that gives AI agents full desktops, including the Cua Spaces app, Cua Driver for native app automation, Lume for local macOS VMs, a cross-platform SDK/CLI for sandboxes, CUA-S1 models, and Cua Bench for evaluation.
keywords: run ai agent on my mac
summary.what_it_does: The repository bundles several components for giving AI agents control of computers. Cua Driver lets agents inspect and operate native desktop apps and browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux through a CLI, MCP, or typed SDKs, with background delivery that can avoid moving the pointer when the platform supports it. Lume creates and manages local macOS and Linux VMs on Apple Silicon using Apple's Virtualization.Framework. The cua SDK and CLI provide one API for local VMs, containers, and machines running cua-spacesd, with Python, TypeScript, and Rust bindings. Cua Spaces is a desktop app (macOS 26 or later, with Linux and Windows cores) that runs agent desktops on your Mac, your own machines, or your own cloud. Cua Bench builds computer-use tasks, evaluates agents, and exports trajectories, and the repo also contains CUA-S1 small models for form-filling decisions with source-only training and evaluation code.
use_cases: let an AI agent operate desktop apps like Calculator or LibreOffice
create local macOS or Linux VMs on Apple Silicon
run isolated sandboxes for agent code execution
host a desktop on a spare Mac for agents
automate form filling with small specialized models
how_to_run: Install Cua Spaces on macOS 26 or later with the curl installer, or download the signed .dmg or .pkg
Install Cua Driver: /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL ...)" on macOS/Linux, or irm ... | iex in PowerShell on Windows
Install Lume with the curl-based installer, then create a VM from an Apple restore image
Install the SDK and CLI with the curl (macOS/Linux) or PowerShell (Windows) installer, then run: cua sb create ubuntu --name dev
Install Cua Bench: uv tool install 'cua-bench[browser]' then uv tool run --from 'cua-bench[browser]' playwright install chromium
Python SDK alternative: pip install cua
notable: Cua Driver operates native apps and browsers across macOS, Windows, and Linux, with background delivery that can avoid taking focus
Lume runs macOS and Linux VMs on Apple Silicon via Apple's Virtualization.Framework
Cua Spaces teleports signed-in apps into a Space, with secrets kept encrypted on the Mac and shared only after approval
Cua Bench can run a simulated task that needs no VM, Docker, or model API key
Mixed licensing: most of the repo is MIT, but Cua Spaces and Cua Driver Bench are FSL-1.1-MIT, and some optional components carry AGPL terms
caveats: Cua Spaces and Cua Driver Bench are source-available under FSL-1.1-MIT, not MIT; the cua-perception extension is not MIT and has AGPL-3.0 obligations
Lume requires Apple Silicon and creates macOS VMs from Apple restore images; Cua Spaces requires macOS 26 or later for the installer path
Several packages are deprecated and unmaintained (cuabot has known security issues and should not be run), and the Swift and Kotlin SDK bindings are not yet released
Pro and Teams Spaces tiers are paid ($18/month and $30 per seat/month); Spaces is free for individuals
